description: The pie chart represents the distribution of mathematical problems across different educational levels and subjects, as curated and categorized by Odyssey Math Data. The chart is divided into 14 slices, each representing a different subject area and educational level. The largest slice, accounting for 21.19% (82 problems), is for Algebra at the Olympiad level. The second largest, at 17.83% (69 problems), is for Algebra at the High School level. This is followed by Pre-Calculus at the High School level with 14.21% (55 problems), and Geometry at the Olympiad level with 6.46% (25 problems). The remaining slices represent subjects at the University level, with Calculus and Analysis at 6.20% (24 problems), Differential Equations at 3.62% (14 problems), Probability at 5.43% (21 problems), Statistics at 4.39% (17 problems), and Number Theory at 1.03% (4 problems). The chart does not include a legend, and the percentages are labeled inside the slices. The slices are not visually emphasized in any particular way.
